topics.topic_label: EU AI Act (Germany's KI-MIG in force 28 July names the Bundesnetzagentur as national market-surveillance authority four days before the 2 August application date; ISO 42001 is explicitly not presumption of conformity)

Governance as a product line (microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit covers 10/10 of the OWASP Agentic Top 10 and gains 8.9% in a day; Swiss governance hiring now spans consulting, retail, pharma and banking)

EU AI Act (two LinkedIn Pulse pieces take opposite positions on the 2 August date three days out — full high-risk enforcement versus Annex III / Article 11 obligations pushed to December 2027 by the Digital Omnibus with inventory duties untouched)

Vendor governance as a business line (LangSmith Gateway ships spend caps, rate limits and PII redaction as product; AIGen generates SPDX 3.0 AI Bills of Materials against the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001; Grant Thornton becomes the second audit firm this quarter to staff a standing AI-security practice)

EU AI Act (Article 50 transparency obligations apply from 2 August across four cases — direct interaction, AI-generated content, emotion recognition and biometric categorisation, deepfakes and public-interest text — binding deployers as well as providers, carrying fines to EUR 15M or 3% of worldwide turnover, and explicitly not delayed by the omnibus; Commission enforcement powers activate the same day)

Vendor governance as a business line (LGT posts an AI Operations Specialist for FinOps — tracking cost at API-call and token granularity, model right-sizing, and KPIs for AI spend — which is cost governance rather than risk governance and a shape this pipeline has not recorded before; SIX meets its governance demand with a fixed-term contract, the first temporary AI-governance posting seen)

EU AI Act (Article 50 applies from 2 August and the Commission opens a complaints tool, a whistleblower tool and a downstream-GPAI channel, with ceilings of €35M/7% and €15M/3%; systems already on the market get until 2 December 2026 for machine-readable marking; three widely-shared LinkedIn posts give three incompatible accounts)

Vendor governance as a business line (Cequence ships AI Discovery plus API, LLM and Skill registries that find shadow agents and MCP servers by mining security logs; 'a fully populated audit trail is not evidence that review happened'; Hardoon works the arithmetic against questionnaire-based governance at fleet scale)

Implementation & deployment revenue (Unique AI hires a Team Lead for an already-existing Global Forward Deployed Data Science team, with staffing responsibility and 1:1s — FDE acquires a management layer; Thinking Machines' open-model finetuning service reportedly does hundreds of millions in annual revenue)

EU AI Act enforcement (day two opens on model-linked cyber incidents, not deepfake labels; procedural non-cooperation — refusing an information request or blocking an evaluation — is independently fineable; a public Complaint Tool and confidential Whistleblower Tool are live)

Governance as a product line (SonarSource sells 'AI code verification and governance' and is hiring engineers to build circuit breakers, sandboxes and trust telemetry — governance hired for as product engineering, not compliance; AISPA audits 3,249 system-prompt instructions across 88 commercial products; BaFin gains AI supervision over banks and insurers)

EU AI Act enforcement (Article 50 liability attaches to the *deployer*, not the vendor — Joule, Agentforce, Now Assist and Copilot all leave the €15M-or-3% exposure with the customer; and the common read that 'the Omnibus delayed everything' is wrong in the two places carrying the most reputational risk, because the CSAM/NCII prohibition and the marking grace-period expiry both land 2 December 2026)

Governance as a product line (an ex-Deloitte auditor open-sources the whole SOC 2 method aimed at AI products — the best-performing Show HN of the day; Julius Baer hires an architect whose deliverable is Architecture Decision Records approved at architecture boards; NetHope ships a pre-adoption PESTLE due-diligence guide)

Governance as a product line (Anaconda's second acquisition in three weeks buys pre-deployment red-teaming, runtime guardrails and NIST/EU-AI-Act compliance automation — governance bolted onto a distribution platform rather than sold as a service; Stanford's AI Index supplies the demand curve, AI-specific governance roles up 17% and firms with no responsible-AI policy down from 24% to 11%, with implementation still blocked by knowledge gaps at 59%)

Vendor governance as a business line (governance stopped being a compliance cost and became a product SKU from three directions in one week - Snowflake and Databricks sell the control plane, Anthropic sells real-time DLP inference hooks for Enterprise, and the first Swiss AI-governance JD read end to end turns out to be a legal role: law degree, CIPP/E-CIPM-AIGP, German and English, and not one technical requirement)

Vendor governance as a product line (ServiceNow's AI Control Tower hits GA covering discover/observe/govern/secure/measure with an MCP gateway in front of all customer MCP transactions, Traceloop-derived runtime agent observability, five NIST- and EU-AI-Act-mapped risk frameworks and a Veza real-time kill switch; Mistral open-sources Shieldstral, a 3B Apache-2.0 guard model re-policied by natural-language question at inference time; Salesforce clears DoD IL5 — governance became a product SKU the same month it became a fine)

Vendor governance as a product line (Snowflake Cortex AI Gateway plus Agent Identity and AI-SPM at GA, ServiceNow AI Control Tower GA, Google staffing an 'AI Analytics, Trust and Verification' PM in Zürich)

Vendor governance as a product line (ServiceNow's AI Control Tower reaches GA with a kill switch for misbehaving agents, Google ships per-agent identity with full operation logging, Mistral open-weights a 3B safety classifier and IBM pairs OpenAI models with its own Autonomous Security — governance is now something vendors sell, not something buyers build)
